body:
Update:

Was able to get it working:  Now resources can be deleted, copied and duplicated and the correct amount of copies will be displayed! This applies to both Local and 'Global' resources!

For Scene instantiation however, it's a bit more tricky, there are more edge cases to cover, and sometimes it tries to count twice.

The only downside is that projects created in a pre-merge version (possibly the ones prior to 4.6) will not keep accurate count of Resources.

But I'm glad it is functioning properly decently at least!

Please make sure your code is formatted properly locally before pushing again if you want checks to run, see [here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/development/code_style_guidelines.html#using-clang-format-locally)

I'll think more about this, but I suppose it'd be best to track external and internal resources differently 

So the counter idea would be scrapped, being replaced by an icon instead.

If either the resource is external or the _current scene_ has multiple instances of the same resource, it will show up the `make_unique` option beside it. 

Because basically the issue with my current approach stems from trying to track down External Resources and them being in every nook and cranny of the engine (Everything is resources loool). Technically it'd be possible of marking every place they appear, but they wouldn't be properly tracked if you drag and dropped them from a previous project, or used a previous version of the engine.

> So the counter idea would be scrapped, being replaced by an icon instead.

I do much prefer the counter - perhaps there's a middle ground that still offers one without the effort of tracking scene-external link counts. Maybe it could display the scene-local link count if it's internal, and then if it's external, make it instead read `N` or `Ext` or something?

Local duplicated Resources now have a counter External Resources use an icon, and can be turned into local if clicked: ![AAAAAAAAAA](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a38e4699-5432-4dd9-9650-7cf706c5658b) Sadly, despite 5 days trying to get it to work, Subresources will not use the counter (unless a way is found ofc). It works pretty unreliably: ![Why](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e0ffa9a-0551-4553-81ba-a02c19196b54) Kinda upsetting, since that is mostly why I decided to make this PR. Will make the finishing touches needed , will try to indicate that making subresources unique is sorta pointless, and will leave it as is for review. EDIT: Maybe I could in fact track the amount of sub resources locally, but it wouldn't do much more than that, unless you made their parent Resource unique

> Adds an icon on the side of a resource if it is not unique.

> Move Make Unique and Make Unique recursive to Icons



Makes sense to take into account concerns raised in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102196:

> User feedback has shown that this change isn't always a clear improvement, because:

> The icon eats up horizontal space that's already limited here, cutting the text or previews significantly.
> It breaks user expectations to no longer have load options next to Clear/Save/etc.

The icon for sub resources is more of a suggestion, one I'm particularly not that fond of. Maybe changing the theme of The Sub resource to indicate that? Or maybe adding a notification when trying to make that resource unique?

I think the main (and most difficult) thing that should be done first it to detect amount of references to a resource.
On UI side:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10319#issuecomment-2257684458 - this is for sure.
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/904#issuecomment-634874239 - looks great in theory but clashed with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109458#issuecomment-3190637574 so I don't have any idea how to make it suitable for everyone.

(Please note that this is my personal opinion, and it may not coincide with the opinion of the Godot team members.)
Edge Cases aside, I'm done with this PR and it's ready for review! (I'm tired help)

Hey everyone, small update: Reinforced Support for Subresources, so they're taken into account when making external ones unique, and also when they're deleted with the parent. Arrays/Dictionaries are also using the counter now.
The PR is in a functional state, besides some quirks, so It's 'okay' for use (at least for my projects). This PR def needs some refactoring, perhaps some optimization ,reducing recursion calls, but I'll force myself to take a break from it until Godot 4.6 starts development, around the time someone from the Godot team might actually take a look at this.  

Note (mostly to self): Subresources in this PR are treated as inseparable from their parents, as it's impossible for a Resource and its nested child not have the same Nodes referencing them. So I took advantage of this when needed to keep better track of Subresources' counter. Also, dont use Vscode for git, it suckssss

Showing a generic Make Unique icon might be too implicit for a shared indicator, this feature is aimed at people who are already confused. Reddit user HyperGameDev suggested a chain link icon (🔗). Maybe LinkButton.svg or Unlinked.svg could work?

@trickster721 maybe that'd be useful, but since Local Resources are indicated with a counter, using 🔗 only for external Resources would be weird imo. Maybe we could use another icon to indicate it's an external resource

Ah, I misunderstood the changes. Right now, when you create a new (unique) resource, you see this: (The tooltip doesn't match the actions that are available. And the right-click recursive action is new, right? In that case, it should probably also be added to the dropdown menu.) I know people are used to the way Blender handles this, but just showing a number with no immediate context feels like it goes against Godot's beginner-friendly style. Blender can be very dense and cryptic. As a beginner, I might read that as "this shape has one circle". Most of the complaints about Make Unique I'm seeing in discussions seem to be from users who are just looking for godotengine/godot-proposals#904, an indicator that appears to warn them when a resource is shared, and editing it could be destructive. https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/comments/1naylu5/why_is_make_unique_the_most_painful_feature_in/ I think displaying the number of references is extraneous, and might be information overload for people who are already struggling and annoyed with the whole concept of references. The specific number seems more like an "FYI", so personally I'd rather see it in the tooltip, like in this example (not a screenshot of the PR): Maybe just solving the first proposal isn't what this PR is about, but I think there's a lot of appetite for it, and the simpler version seems like an easy win.

@trickster721 I think those are very good points! I didn't even think adding a counter could result in a UX issue (something I was actually trying to improve on about Godot 😅)

> (The tooltip doesn't match the actions that are available. And the right-click recursive action is new, right? In that case, it should probably also be added to the dropdown menu.)
> 

Another oversight on my end. I disable the option of making a resource unique if there's only one instance of it (this solves https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10319) To indicate that, I used a counter and made it look greyed out.  So it isn't totally due people wanting a blender-like counter (though it's a major part of the reason)

Still, I really liked your idea (specially your mock up) and I think the counter show on the tooltip pretty Ingenious. Unfortunately, I think I'll leave the maintainers to decide which is better UX-Wise, since heck, maybe the button will even be removed/placed in a different location, as arkology pointed out:

> Makes sense to take into account concerns raised in #102196:

>User feedback has shown that this change isn't always a clear improvement, because:

>The icon eats up horizontal space that's already limited here, cutting the text or previews significantly.
It breaks user expectations to no longer have load options next to Clear/Save/etc.
>
>

Did some refactoring in the hopes of reducing code duplication, but as there are lot of moving parts to this, I had to duplicate some (on the bright side it'd even more if I hadn't tried to refactor). But at least I'm not touching core anymore so its a win! Also I guess it couldn't be helped in some cases **Also, bulk setting Resources is now supported**! One edge case ive found though is that Dictonaries don't show a counter/make unique button when the Resource is the key: I'm not sure why? The options tab doesn't look like a normal resource's too, so Ill see if its just an edge case or something with my code (It also gets linked like any other Resource, so having an indicator is pretty important)

Was able to add indicators to Dictionary keys. The reason they weren't previously present was because Godot makes them not able to be Edited (`edited` in `Resource Picker` == false). So they weren't visible due to that flag. One quirk with it is that you can't make them unique (but this is mostly due to how Godot currently handles Resources as keys so this will now suffice) Also, if you for example, have multiple Nodes Referencing a Resource, and then you add a SubResource to them, now they're counted automatically. Here's an example with Noise Texture ![SubResLove](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc1e36d3-11ee-4f18-a91b-592bc46ca4d7) Decided to add these already mostly bc I think it's best from a reviewer's standpoint to see everything instead of adding it after review and having to review it again.
Please do not push so many times in a row, it's very noisy and causes CI to run unnecessarily
@AThousandShips  I apologize, I was trying to rebase the PR, as it was creating 2 commits when syncing the branch.

It may not be that relevant, but I believe that in addition to that, a feature should also be added than when enabling uniqueness for a resource, using different color to highlight the make unique option to indicate that the resource has been  made unique would also be very helpful for users, too.

@MadeScientist It'd be good to add that as well, but I believe it would overlap with how SubResources are indicated in the editor

I've encountered an issue while testing the disable feature:

- Resources with Arrays/Dictionaries with Subresources cannot have the `make_unique` disabled, since we'd need to have the Reference to its parent, but `Resource_Owner` is pointing to its Array/Dictionary.  We'd have to come up with some way to check if there is a Resource parent.

![sdad](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e694528-c2a4-4173-bbe3-3400a1ff6c72)

@Calinou  I'd like to ask your opinion concerning what arkology reminded:

> > Adds an icon on the side of a resource if it is not unique.
> > Move Make Unique and Make Unique recursive to Icons
> 
> Makes sense to take into account concerns raised in #102196:
> 
> > User feedback has shown that this change isn't always a clear improvement, because:
> > The icon eats up horizontal space that's already limited here, cutting the text or previews significantly.
> > It breaks user expectations to no longer have load options next to Clear/Save/etc.

Would you believe having a button alongside the Resource would raise the same concerns pointed out? would removing options `make_unique` and `make_unique_recursive`  and moving them to the button be too disruptive?

> Would you believe having a button alongside the Resource would raise the same concerns pointed out? would removing options `make_unique` and `make_unique_recursive` and moving them to the button be too disruptive?

Thinking about it again, I agree the button currently added in this PR will be an issue in some cases. Since it acts off a single click, it could also be prone to misclicks resulting in users making resources built-in without realizing it.

But I guess the same could be said about the undo button that resets the property to its original value?  I think misclicking would be a non issue, because it would be clearly indicated to the user (the button being greyed out, the counter showing '1') if an accident like that happens.

I'm more concerned about whether the button takes too much space. If not, we could maybe discuss changing the number to a chain icon, like argued here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109458#issuecomment-3272488648, mostly this:

>Most of the complaints about Make Unique I'm seeing in discussions seem to be from users who are just looking for godotengine/godot-proposals#904, an indicator that appears to warn them when a resource is shared, and editing it could be destructive.

> I think displaying the number of references is extraneous, and might be information overload for people who are already struggling and annoyed with the whole concept of references. The specific number seems more like an "FYI", so personally I'd rather see it in the tooltip, like in this example (not a screenshot of the PR):

Refactored so Disabling and Enabling duplication works more seemingly, also added better descriptions as to why an option couldn't be used.
Furthermore I decided to implement https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109458#issuecomment-3272488648, as:
- The counter is more of a 'secondary' information and should thus be accessed by hovering the button.
- The icon should be descriptive of the feature, and (for external resources at least), a `make_unique` icon wasn't cutting it (it would also be weird imo to have a counter for internal Resources and use a chain icon🔗  exclusively to external ones)

Feel free to express your agreement or disagreement towards this change! 

![showtime](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7bcf932-af63-4540-898d-5a5be884be91)


One problem with the button accepting input however, is that it gets disabled as soon as make it unique. This is not a problem for Resources with no nesting, but for nested Resources, you either `make_unique_recursive` right off the bat or it disappears with `make_unique.` This might be a non issue but I decided to mention that


![showtime2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53dd72c3-7bb3-4190-a446-925595206546)


Also, to fully implement https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10319 I'd have to tinker with the `Make_Unique_Recursive `popup, by disabling uniqueness if it's already been made unique, but I'll leave that to a next PR

I gave it a bit testing and it seems to work fine overall. One issue I found is the note about sub-resources: It appears regardless if the resource has sub-resources or not and right-click will open the unique recursive dialog with single entry. The Make Unique button does nothing for MultiNodeEdit. It's because the Resource is made unique and set for all nodes at once, so it's still being shared. I think the button should be disabled in that case (the context menu does not have Make Unique too). Same for Dictionary keys. EDIT: So for multinode, it still makes sense if the Resource is used in other nodes. This is tricky. Maybe check if usage count is equal to number of nodes? But I guess that's unreliable. Speaking of the button... It takes space. It's similar to the quick load button, which users weren't very happy about. Though it only shows in specific cases, so probably it's fine?

Noticing that there are places where `TTR` is applied to variables like `TTR(tooltip)`, that won't work AFAIK as the string won't be extractable, `TTR` should be around raw strings so the content can be extracted for translation data

> Noticing that there are places where `TTR` is applied to variables like `TTR(tooltip)`, that won't work AFAIK as the string won't be extractable, `TTR` should be around raw strings so the content can be extracted for translation data

Yes, tooltip text should be handled differently for sure.

I did a code review. I didn't delve very deep into the implementation, at glance it looks ok. It's limited only to editor code, which is good.

The only concern is scanning all properties whenever object/array/dictionary is changed. I did test some cases that I think could be heavily affected and didn't notice any big slowdowns, so it's not as bad as it looks.

Also the code duplication. OBJECT/ARRAY/DICTIONARY is a famous trio in inspector-related code. I've seen the same methods many times already, but since they always do something a bit different, it's difficult to really unify it :/

Thanks for you guys Input! > I gave it a bit testing and it seems to work fine overall. One issue I found is the note about sub-resources This is most likely due to how External Resources are checked for recursive uniqueness, I'll take a look on that. But the main idea is that `make_unique_recursive` is only enabled if there's at least one subresource `A` that's either external or has multiple copies.
As for the MultiNodeEdit: > So for multinode, it still makes sense if the Resource is used in other nodes. This is tricky. Maybe check if usage count is equal to number of nodes? But I guess that's unreliable.
In that case, it's pretty difficult to determine how to proceed. My initial idea would be to have https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13163 implemented so `Make Unique` actually duplicates for each Node instead of making only of copy that is shared between selected Nodes. Then, I guess we could enable/disable MultiNodeEdit using these: - To enable duplicating property `A`, we must find at least a Node from selection which shares Resource `A` with another Node in the Tree. Then, we duplicate this Resource the amount necessary, while leaving the others Nodes whose `A` is already unique alone. - If `A` is already unique for all Nodes in a selection, disable it.
> It takes space. It's similar to the quick load button, which users weren't very happy about. Though it only shows in specific cases, so probably it's fine? That was one of my worries, but currently there's no way to indicate that if not by an icon. Reduz's puts a counter on here, which is a really weird design IMO and not rly descriptive.

> The only concern is scanning all properties whenever object/array/dictionary is changed. I did test some cases that I think could be heavily affected and didn't notice any big slowdowns, so it's not as bad as it looks. Yeah it's wasteful currently, removing Resources only to re-add them again, with the exception of the one that changed, but covering all possible cases an Array/Dictionary can change would be pretty painful 😅
--- > Noticing that there are places where TTR is applied to variables like TTR(tooltip), that won't work AFAIK as the string won't be extractable, TTR should be around raw strings so the content can be extracted for translation data @AThousandShips is there a way to circumvent this? My previous approach was changing the tooltip text directly after a set of conditions were met, and there was a lot of overlap (e.g A external Resource with Subresources vs an Internal Resources with Subresouces share more of less the same message).
For TTR, see my suggestions: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109458#discussion_r2437364028

Added the required changes. For MultiNodeEdit i decided to check the Node selection against the Resource counter. If they're equal or if the edited resource is not external, you're not allowed to make them unique.

Therefore a more fine-tuned solution for this can flourish. Since I guess, as it stands now, making many Resources unique in bulk like that is pretty niche,  specially since it might break user expectations of what this means, the current solution is fine?

![blenda](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c947f96-ae98-499e-a4bf-9b965fe97cc5)

I'm not sure how to circumvent this without having an icon of sorts. Long term we could refactor the UI so it accepts more buttons or shinks appropriately. Any suggestions are appreciated, but idk if there's something to be done

Will wait to push the Rebased commit, but what I did in this one is to remove the Resource icon if there is a preview and the button's size meets a certain threshold: ![showff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8debfb38-3311-4398-ba89-3b1440f66365) This is the least intrusive approach I could find. The previous ones involved either increasing the minimum inspector size to accommodate all buttons or removing the preview altogether. Although, it's worth pointing out that the preview is usually not helpful for bigger sprites. I didn't remove the preview however bc 3D meshes seem to be more helpful even when the inspector's size is pretty small: I also solved an edge case where saved to disk resources would be included in the hash map if it was previously built in. EDIT: Rebased

I'm so, so glad this PR exists! I've been trying to build a GDscript based prototype around the start of this year (even consulted with the dev chat and passivestar about it) but failed to find the time to bring it forward. The inability to understand which resources were non-unique has been a great pain point for my team, it brought upon us so many hard to understand interactions. Thank you so much!

P.s. I don't think it will be very useful at this point, but here is my attempt for reference https://github.com/farfalk/resource-users-addon. There is an attempt to deal with external resources shared among scenes in the whole project, with a hint to implement a resource database in the .godot folder

@farfalk I'm really happy this PR is being of great use! 
As for external Resources, I had looked into your code as well as trying other approaches to the problem, but I couldn't really bring them to work. One of my ideas at the time was to imitate how Godot's save global groups, but I couldn't get much out of it.

Nerverheless, since counting external Resources is most useful only when you want to look up which Nodes are using it, it seems this PR can currently do without it.
I think currently the only advantage to implement this as it stands now would be to unify some code between external internal Resources inside Resource picker, but it's rather trivial
